items.item: Recommends measuring/profiling first and comparing before/after
Replaces per-enemy scripts with one manager loop
Replaces Humanoids with lightweight server-side movement (CFrame/position along path) and client-side rendering/interpolation
Replaces Touched-based damage with server-side range/spatial checks
Addresses rendering cost on mobile (model pooling, LOD/animation reduction)
Preserves the intended experience (doesn't just cap enemy count without discussing it)

slop: Stray 'Apex: performance → genres' header with no meaning for the user
Calls the data approach 'the standard Roblox approach' without support

incorrect_or_stale: Client positions computed from os.clock() - spawnTime: os.clock is local CPU time and not synced with the server, so workspace:GetServerTimeNow() is needed
BulkMoveTo mode advice is backwards: FireCFrameChanged is the cheaper mode, and FireAllEvents is the one to avoid
Setting Massless = true on anchored, non-physics parts does nothing for performance
slop: Humanoid tuning list (HumanoidRigType, RequiresNeck, SetStateEnabled for everything) is generic and contradicts its own advice to remove Humanoids
Suggests StreamingEnabled while admitting it doesn't apply to a fixed-camera TD
'Stagger spawns' changes wave design without discussing the gameplay effect
overengineering: Offers several targeting options at once (GetPartBoundsInRadius, squared distances against the table, a spatial grid) without picking one

raw.reason: A is accurate throughout, profiles first and re-measures after each step, uses GetServerTimeNow correctly for client sync, and talks about keeping the gameplay intact, while B has real API mistakes (os.clock for sync, BulkMoveTo modes backwards) and some generic filler.
